markdown_report:
The strongest next experiment is a **sequence-normalized 0.5 terminal/reconstruction objective mixture**, with a small gradient audit. At 30% progress, this provides a feasible training hypothesis before introducing adaptive gradient surgery.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** First, Electronics has weaker sampled-pair separation, including a negative tenth-percentile margin. These training measurements motivate investigation but establish neither the cause nor validation performance. Second, serving parity is unavailable because category identity propagation failed. Repairing that diagnostic integration is necessary before interpreting history interventions; incorrect exported predictions have not been demonstrated. Third, terminal and reconstruction examples can contain different numbers of supervised targets. Equal example frequency therefore need not imply equal objective influence.

**Insights from related work.** BERT4Rec [1] supplies bidirectional masked reconstruction and appended-mask prediction. The RSS study [2] discusses their weak correspondence, supporting a supervision-alignment hypothesis without proving objective conflict. PCGrad [3] motivates measuring negative gradient inner products, while GradNorm [4] motivates measuring gradient magnitudes separately. Neither establishes that adaptive balancing will improve this benchmark.

These observations define three directions: serving verification, objective normalization, and interference measurement. Their conceptual map is:

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Unresolved gap |
|---|---|---|
| Verification | Reloaded-checkpoint parity | Category identity blocks measurement |
| Alignment | Reconstruction versus terminal masking | Unknown validation benefit |
| Optimization | Gradient cosine and norms | Unknown functional transfer |

Three candidate algorithms follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sequence-normalized fixed mixture [1,2] | 4/7/3 | Simple, interpretable alignment experiment | Established components; normalization changes require a control |
| Equal-norm gradient transfer probe [3,4] | 5/6/5 | Tests local functional interference | Local effects may not predict generalization |
| PCGrad between objectives [3] | 3/6/6 | Directly addresses measured conflict | Premature without persistent harmful interference |

For the selected mixture, sample users and training endpoints using the corrected baseline policy. Assign exactly half of each even-sized batch to terminal-only masking; retain the corrected reconstruction policy for the remainder. Average supervised-target losses within each example, then average examples. This gives equal objective coefficients without claiming equal gradient influence. Retain the baseline loss function and negative sampler.

```python
for sequence, branch in balanced_training_examples():
    x, targets = baseline_masking(sequence, branch)
    loss = baseline_target_loss(model(x), targets).mean()
    accumulate_example_loss(loss)
optimize(mean_example_loss())
```

Compare against reconstruction-only training with the same sequence reduction, documenting the corrected baseline’s original reduction separately. Audit paired objective gradients on a small fixed training-prefix sample. Preserve one BERT4Rec checkpoint per category, all serving interfaces, appended MASK, final nonpadding readout, fixed seeds and training limits. Select exclusively by unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10; no improvement is currently demonstrated.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643; [3] https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.06782; [4] https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.02257.

idea.description: Test a fixed 0.5 mixture of terminal-only and corrected-baseline reconstruction examples, normalizing loss within each sequence before averaging sequences. Use a small paired gradient audit to distinguish objective coefficients from actual gradient influence.
idea.motivation: Appended-mask serving differs from interior masked reconstruction, but no supplied evidence establishes harmful objective conflict. Controlling example frequency and loss reduction yields an interpretable experiment while preserving the corrected BERT4Rec backbone. Existing training margins and qualitative feedback motivate this hypothesis without demonstrating its benefit.
idea.implementation_notes:
Keep the corrected model architecture, baseline target loss, negative sampler, user sampling and endpoint policy. For an even batch size, randomly assign exactly half the examples to terminal-only training and half to corrected-baseline reconstruction using training seed 42. Terminal examples contain only the preceding history and reserved MASK at the selected endpoint; no later items or unmasked shifted targets enter their bidirectional input. Reconstruction examples retain the supplied all-MASK target policy. Require at least one supervised target per example. Compute each example's mean target loss, then average examples; report branch example counts, target counts, loss sums and reduction definitions. Equal coefficients do not imply equal gradient norms.

Compare to a reconstruction-only control using the same per-sequence reduction. Record the original corrected-baseline reduction explicitly: if it differs, the comparison to that original baseline cannot isolate mixture composition alone. Each experimental arm trains fresh category models; never reuse another trial's checkpoint or combine predictions. Predeclare the comparison and avoid expanding the search based solely on noisy diagnostics.

On a small fixed set of public training prefixes, compute terminal and reconstruction gradients separately at the same checkpoint in evaluation mode, with gradients enabled but no optimizer update. Report blockwise cosine, both norms, norm ratio, negative-cosine frequency and zero-gradient counts; restore model mode and RNG states afterward. These measurements remain descriptive and do not trigger PCGrad in this experiment.

Repair explicit category identity propagation to ModelView. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Return measured metrics and definitions with unavailable results represented explicitly. Verify exact checkpoint-state identity and internal/exported prediction parity on short, full, truncated and batched histories before interpreting sensitivity; avoid runtime source introspection for dynamically loaded classes.

Keep Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and trial-local artifacts. Keep checkpoint configuration and predictor writer synchronized. Serving retains the latest maxlen-1 interactions, appends reserved MASK and reads its actual final nonpadding index, never count-1. Each category loads exactly one trained checkpoint. Retain five training-user full-catalog unseen-item recommendations per category. Use only available histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. Account for every training and diagnostic attempt within 43,200 GPU-seconds; leave selection and held-out evaluation to the unchanged host protocol.
idea.pseudocode:
preregister mixture and reconstruction-only control
for category in four_required_categories:
    initialize corrected BERT4Rec with seed 42
    for epoch in range(at_most_200):
        for step in range(200):
            examples = sample_baseline_users_and_training_endpoints()
            branches = seeded_shuffle(equal_terminal_and_reconstruction_labels)
            losses = []
            for example, branch in zip(examples, branches):
                if branch == TERMINAL:
                    sequence, targets = prefix_plus_reserved_MASK(example)
                else:
                    sequence, targets = corrected_baseline_reconstruction(example)
                assert targets_are_masked_and_nonempty(sequence, targets)
                target_losses = unchanged_baseline_loss(model(sequence), targets)
                losses.append(target_losses.mean())
                record_branch_example_and_target_counts(branch, targets)
            optimizer_step(stack(losses).mean())
    save_one_category_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor_configuration()
    verify_reload_identity_and_exported_serving_parity()
    run_small_paired_gradient_audit_without_parameter_updates()
return artifacts_for_unchanged_host_macro_validation_HR10

originality.positive: Makes the proposed terminal/reconstruction mixture scientifically interpretable through explicit example weighting, target-count accounting and a matched reduction control.
originality.negative: Combines established masked-training objectives and loss normalization; it introduces no new backbone or optimization principle.

future_potential.positive: Can establish a reproducible basis for later objective-alignment and gradient-interference studies within a single sequential model.
future_potential.negative: Neither the supplied diagnostics nor the cited studies establish validation gains from this particular mixture.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the corrected encoder, target loss and inference computation; the main training changes concern branch allocation and loss reduction.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable attribution still requires sampler provenance, a matched control, export parity and careful gradient-audit accounting.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item reconstruction for sequential recommendation and appended-mask next-item prediction.
Provides the architectural foundation preserved by this proposal.
limitations: Does not establish the best terminal/reconstruction mixture for the pinned four-category benchmark.
Its objectives alone do not establish harmful gradient interference.

related_work.title: Effective and Efficient Training for Sequential Recommendation using Recency Sampling
contributions: Discusses weak correspondence between random masked reconstruction and next-item prediction.
Motivates examining how training examples align with the serving task.
limitations: Does not demonstrate that a fixed 0.5 mixture improves this RecHarness task.
Does not establish gradient conflict between the proposed branches.

related_work.title: Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
contributions: Introduces PCGrad to modify conflicting task gradients.
Motivates measuring gradient inner products before proposing conflict-specific interventions.
limitations: Negative gradient cosine alone does not establish harmful transfer or validation degradation.
Its findings do not directly validate gradient surgery for this BERT4Rec experiment.

related_work.title: GradNorm: Gradient Normalization for Adaptive Loss Balancing in Deep Multitask Networks
contributions: Uses gradient magnitudes to adapt multitask loss weighting.
Supports distinguishing nominal loss coefficients from measured optimization influence.
limitations: Equal gradient norms need not imply optimal recommendation performance.
Adaptive weighting adds experimental complexity beyond the selected fixed-mixture hypothesis.
